kind: code (tier A: 2 lenses + skeptics on majors; phase-gate red-team-by-data >=20 deny spellings). Subagents read §3.5 (1334-1427) — the git deny matrix is normative; NEVER paraphrase it.

assertions.text: decideGit(command, sessionRole, gitMode, runActive, branchPolicy) -> {action: allow|deny, reason?}; DEFAULT-DENY for any subcommand not in the read-only allow-list or an explicit row
the FULL §3.5 matrix as a table, one test per row

verbatim guards: git add src/config.ts deny naming conductor_publish; git log --grep config allow; git stash push -m drop deny; git stash list allow; git commit -m "fix reset logic" deny-with-publish-reason (not destructive-verb false positive); echo hi && git reset --hard deny (every segment scanned); newline-separated compound deny; +refspec/:refspec push denies; restore --staged allow vs restore --staged --worktree deny

one test each: git apply patch.diff deny (most important row); worktree add deny; update-ref, symbolic-ref, sparse-checkout set, submodule update, bisect start, gc --prune=now, reflog expire, fetch, remote set-url, tag -d v1, config user.email x all deny
git blame, shortlog, describe, cat-file -p HEAD, rev-list --count HEAD, worktree list, config --get user.name all allow
invented subcommand git frobnicate denies by default with reason naming the subcommand
git switch feature: deny under branchPolicy pin with run active; allow under check-only; allow under pin with no active run

phaseGate1Bindings.source: Phase 1 adversarial gate (correctness + counterexample lenses, multiple independent contexts)
MUST: The deny matrix MUST match over the FULL parsed token segment, NOT solely gitSubcommand's single-word return. Two-word discriminators are load-bearing: stash list (allow) vs stash push/drop (deny); worktree list (allow) vs worktree add (deny); remote -v (allow) vs remote add/set-url (deny); config --get/--list (allow) vs config <k> <v> (deny); reflog show (allow) vs reflog expire (deny); branch [list] (allow) vs branch -d/-D/-M (deny); checkout <branch> vs checkout --/checkout ./multi-operand/checkout -b (deny); restore --staged (allow) vs restore --staged --worktree (deny).

REQUIRED test (the dangerous false-ALLOW the gate exists to prevent): `git branch -D x` MUST deny even though its primary subcommand 'branch' is on the read-only allow-list. Keying the allow decision on gitSubcommand alone would allow it.

After the Phase-1 primitive hardening, gitSubcommand returns a deny-forcing token for unrecognized global flags; 5.1 must still default-deny any subcommand not on the exhaustive read-only allow-list (the invented-subcommand test: `git frobnicate` denies).

5.1 must exercise the git-detection hardening: `A=b git push`, `env git push`, `command git apply x`, `sudo git push`, `/usr/bin/git push` are all git-write commands that MUST be detected and denied (isGitCommand now skips env-assignment prefixes + env/command/sudo wrappers + resolves path basenames). Backtick-substitution and alias-injection residuals are DOCUMENTED in honest-limits-pending.md (G7), not asserted as caught.
phaseGate1Bindings.redTeamByData: The Phase 5 red-team-by-data probe (>=20 deny spellings) MUST include: value-flag globals (git --namespace log push, git --work-tree /x rm), env/wrapper prefixes, and the two-word allow/deny boundary pairs above. The orchestrator executes all against decideGit and compares to expected verdicts.
